questions.prompt: When a vehicle is stopped to allow a pedestrian to cross the road, other vehicles that are approaching from the rear:
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian. The stopped vehicle may hide the pedestrian from your view. Key words: "it is illegal".

choices.text: May pass the stopped vehicle when the pedestrian crossing signal has changed to "Don't Walk"
May pass the stopped vehicle when eye contact is made with the pedestrian and the pedestrian stops
Must not pass the stopped vehicle
May pass the stopped vehicle if there is no oncoming traffic that may impede passing safely

questions.prompt: Why is it not safe to pass a loaded log-haul truck that is turning?
questions.explanation: The logs overhang the back of the truck and swing out wide during a turn, which can sweep across every lane. Stay well back until the turn is finished. Key words: "danger zone", "could block all the lanes".

choices.text: The driver of the truck needs to fully concentrate on the turn and does not need the added responsibility of a passing vehicle
Loaded log-haul trucks obey the 6-second rule for turns
A danger zone exists as the overhang of the logs from the tail end of the truck could block all the lanes on a highway during the turn
It is illegal to do so

questions.prompt: When approaching the rear of a school bus that is displaying alternating flashing amber lights, a driver should:
questions.explanation: Alternating flashing amber lights mean the bus is slowing to stop so students can get on or off. Be prepared to stop: once the red lights flash and the stop arm is out, you must stop.

choices.text: Be prepared to stop as this is a warning that the alternating flashing red lights will come on once the bus has stopped
Stop immediately because the school bus is loading or unloading students
Be prepared to stop as this could be a warning that there is a collision ahead and the traffic flow has stopped
Use caution as the school bus is approaching a railroad crossing and is about to stop

questions.prompt: In an urban area, when a pedestrian is standing at a crosswalk with their arm raised at approximately right angles to their body and pointing to the opposite curb, what does this mean?
questions.explanation: A pedestrian pointing across the road with an outstretched arm is signalling that they want to cross. Drivers must stop and yield. Key words: "urban area", "must stop and yield".

choices.text: Drivers must stop and yield to the pedestrian
The pedestrian is visually impaired and needs assistance to cross the road
Drivers do not have to yield to the pedestrian until they step off the curb
Drivers should reduce speed to 30 km/h and be cautious when passing the pedestrian

questions.prompt: When encountering a funeral procession that is crossing an intersection:
questions.explanation: Let a funeral procession pass through the intersection as a group. Yield and don't cut through the line of vehicles. Key words: "do not break through".

choices.text: Sound the horn before proceeding
Proceed through the funeral procession only when there is sufficient space between vehicles
Yield the right-of-way and do not break through the procession
Flash the high beam headlights before proceeding

questions.prompt: When stopping for a pedestrian at a crosswalk, about how far back should you stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping about two to three car lengths back lets drivers in other lanes see the pedestrian and stop in time. (Driver's Guide p. 97)

choices.text: About 2 to 3 car lengths
Right at the edge of the crosswalk
About 1 metre
About 10 car lengths

questions.prompt: You see a flashing yellow pedestrian-activated light at a crosswalk. What must you do?
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow pedestrian-activated light, slow to 30 km/h and yield to pedestrians who want to cross. (Driver's Guide p. 97)

choices.text: Slow to 30 km/h and yield to pedestrians wanting to cross
Stop only if a pedestrian is already in the crosswalk
Continue at the posted speed; the light is only for pedestrians
Sound your horn to warn pedestrians and continue

questions.prompt: A pedestrian starts crossing at an intersection that has no painted crosswalk lines. What must you do?
questions.explanation: Every intersection has a crosswalk, marked or unmarked, unless a sign says otherwise. Once a pedestrian has entered it, you must yield. (Driver's Guide pp. 41, 97)

choices.text: Yield, because there is an unmarked crosswalk at the intersection
Continue, because pedestrians must use marked crosswalks
Yield only if the intersection has a traffic light
Sound your horn and proceed carefully

questions.prompt: A person walking beside and pushing a bicycle is considered:
questions.explanation: A cyclist who is walking beside and pushing a bicycle is a pedestrian. When riding, the bicycle is a vehicle. (Driver's Guide p. 97)

choices.text: A pedestrian
A cyclist who must follow the rules for vehicles
A slow moving vehicle
A vehicle that must use the bicycle lane

questions.prompt: What is the correct way to pass a cyclist?
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, change lanes as you would to pass any other vehicle. (Driver's Guide p. 98)

choices.text: Change lanes, as you would to pass another vehicle
Stay in your lane and pass as closely as is safe
Sound your horn and pass once the cyclist moves to the curb
Pass on the cyclist's right side

questions.prompt: You are parked at the curb and want to open your door. Who is responsible for making sure it is safe to do so?
questions.explanation: Always check for cyclists before opening your door. It is the driver's responsibility to wait until it is safe. (Driver's Guide p. 98)

choices.text: The driver
Cyclists, who must watch for opening doors
The driver and cyclists share it equally
No one, if the vehicle is legally parked

questions.prompt: In Alberta, who is required by law to wear an approved bicycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Cyclists and passengers on a bicycle who are under 18 years of age must wear an approved bicycle safety helmet. (Driver's Guide p. 97)

choices.text: Cyclists and passengers under 18 years of age
All cyclists, regardless of age
Cyclists under 16 years of age
Only cyclists riding on highways

questions.prompt: A motorcycle ahead of you is riding in the left part of its lane. This most likely means the rider:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders often ride in the left portion of their lane to be more visible. It does not mean they are turning left. (Driver's Guide p. 98)

choices.text: Is positioned to be more visible to other road users
Is preparing to turn left
Wants you to pass on the right
Is about to stop

questions.prompt: May you drive side by side with a motorcycle in the same lane?
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle rider. A motorcycle needs the whole lane to travel safely. (Driver's Guide p. 99)

choices.text: No, a motorcycle needs the whole lane
Yes, if the lane is wide enough
Yes, but only on multi-lane highways
Yes, if the rider waves you past

questions.prompt: You are following a large truck and cannot see either of its side mirrors. What does this tell you?
questions.explanation: If you can't see both of a large vehicle's side mirrors, you are too close, and the driver probably can't see you. If you can see the driver in the mirror, the driver can see you. (Driver's Guide p. 99)

choices.text: You are too close, and the driver probably cannot see you
The truck's mirrors are not adjusted properly
You are at a safe following distance
The truck is about to turn

questions.prompt: A large truck ahead of you is turning right. Where is the most dangerous place for your vehicle to be?
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra room to turn. Stay well back and never drive in the space on the right of a truck that is turning right, or you could be squeezed against the curb. (Driver's Guide p. 99)

choices.text: In the space between the truck and the curb on its right
Several car lengths behind the truck
Well back in the lane to the left of the truck
Stopped behind the truck with a large gap

questions.prompt: A large truck is turning onto the road you are on and may need to use part of your lane. What should you do?
questions.explanation: A large vehicle may need to cross the centre line or use part of your lane to turn. Stop back from the intersection to give it room. (Driver's Guide p. 100)

choices.text: Stop back from the intersection to give it room to turn
Move up to the stop line so the truck driver can see you
Sound your horn to warn the truck driver
Continue, since the truck must stay in its own lane

questions.prompt: The logs on a loaded log hauling truck can extend up to how far beyond the rear of the truck?
questions.explanation: Logs can extend as much as nine metres beyond the rear of the truck, which is why a turning log truck can block every lane. (Driver's Guide p. 100)

choices.text: 9 metres
3 metres
1.5 metres
15 metres

questions.prompt: On a four-lane undivided highway, a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and its stop arm out. Who must stop?
questions.explanation: On an undivided highway, traffic in every lane, in both directions, must stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing. (Driver's Guide p. 101)

choices.text: Traffic in all four lanes, in both directions
Only traffic behind the bus
Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
Only oncoming traffic

questions.prompt: When a school bus has its red lights flashing, about how far away from the bus must you stop?
questions.explanation: Stop about 20 metres (four to five car lengths) away, so drivers behind you can see the lights and the students crossing. (Driver's Guide p. 101)

choices.text: About 20 metres
About 5 metres
About 50 metres
About 100 metres

questions.prompt: On a highway divided by a median, you are approaching a school bus from the front and its red lights are flashing. What should you do?
questions.explanation: On a divided highway, only traffic behind the bus must stop. Traffic approaching from the front may proceed with caution, watching for pedestrians. (Driver's Guide p. 102)

choices.text: Proceed with caution and watch for pedestrians
Stop about 20 metres from the bus
Stop until the red lights are turned off
Speed up to clear the area quickly

questions.prompt: You have stopped for a school bus with its red lights flashing. When may you proceed?
questions.explanation: Remain stopped until the alternating red lights are turned off and the stop sign on the driver's side is no longer extended. (Driver's Guide p. 102)

choices.text: When the red lights are off and the stop arm is no longer extended
As soon as all the students have left the bus
When the bus driver waves you on
After waiting 30 seconds

questions.prompt: A vehicle ahead has flashing amber and red lights and is spraying snow and sand. What is it?
questions.explanation: Snowplows use flashing amber and red lights to be more visible: "flashing amber and red means snowplow ahead". (Driver's Guide p. 102)

choices.text: A snowplow
A school bus that is about to stop
A tow truck
An oversized load

questions.prompt: Where it is safe, snowplow operators move to the side of the road to let traffic pass about every:
questions.explanation: Snowplow operators move over every five to eight kilometres, where it is safe, to let vehicles pass. It is safer to wait for them than to pass. (Driver's Guide p. 102)

choices.text: 5 to 8 kilometres
1 to 2 kilometres
15 to 20 kilometres
50 kilometres

questions.prompt: Passing a snowplow is strictly prohibited when:
questions.explanation: Passing a snowplow is prohibited when the view along its side is obstructed, when passing would impede its operation, or when it can't be done safely. (Driver's Guide p. 102)

choices.text: The view along the side of the snowplow is obstructed
The snowplow is travelling below the speed limit
The snowplow has its flashing lights on
The road is a two-lane highway

questions.prompt: At a railway crossing sign, you must stop if a train is visible or sounding a signal and is approaching within:
questions.explanation: You must stop when a train is visible or sounding a signal and approaching within 500 metres (about five city blocks) of the crossing. (Driver's Guide p. 103)

choices.text: 500 metres of the crossing
100 metres of the crossing
50 metres of the crossing
2 kilometres of the crossing

questions.prompt: At a railway crossing with a stop sign, where must you stop?
questions.explanation: A stop sign at a railway crossing means a complete stop between 5 metres and 15 metres from the nearest rail. Don't proceed until you're sure no train is coming. (Driver's Guide p. 103)

choices.text: Between 5 and 15 metres from the nearest rail
Within 2 metres of the nearest rail
At least 30 metres from the nearest rail
Anywhere before the tracks, as long as you stop

questions.prompt: The lights are flashing and the bells are ringing at a railway crossing. The driver nearest the crossing must stop at least how far from the nearest rail?
questions.explanation: The driver of the vehicle nearest the crossing must stop at least five metres back from the nearest rail, and wait until the lights and bells stop. (Driver's Guide p. 104)

choices.text: 5 metres
1 metre
15 metres
20 metres

questions.prompt: A train has just passed a railway crossing and the gates are starting to rise. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Remain stopped until the gates are fully raised, the lights stop flashing, and the bells stop ringing. Never cross while a gate is down, rising, or lowering. Another train may be coming. (Driver's Guide p. 104)

choices.text: Stay stopped until the gates are up and the lights and bells have stopped
Go as soon as the gates start to rise
Drive around the gates if no other train is visible
Proceed once the last car of the train has passed

questions.prompt: Your vehicle stalls on a railway crossing and a train is approaching. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Get everyone out and away from the tracks. Move toward the direction the train is coming from, so you won't be hit by flying debris if the train strikes the vehicle. (Driver's Guide p. 104)

choices.text: Get everyone out and move away from the tracks, toward the direction the train is coming from
Keep trying to restart the engine
Get everyone out and move away in the direction the train is travelling
Stay in the vehicle with seat belts fastened

questions.prompt: Because of its weight and speed, a light rail transit (LRT) train may need up to how far to stop in an emergency?
questions.explanation: An LRT train may take up to 100 metres to stop in an emergency. LRT trains are also very quiet, so never drive around the gates. (Driver's Guide p. 105)

choices.text: 100 metres
10 metres
30 metres
1 kilometre

questions.prompt: You are driving in a funeral procession with your headlights on. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Drivers in a funeral procession, with headlights on, may continue through a stop sign or red light if they are closely following the vehicle ahead and it is safe. (Driver's Guide p. 105)

choices.text: You may continue through a stop sign or red light if you are closely following the vehicle ahead and it is safe
You must stop at every stop sign and red light like other traffic
You may pass other vehicles in the procession
You don't need your headlights on in daylight

questions.prompt: When passing a large truck on a two-way highway, a driver should:
questions.explanation: When passing a large truck on a two-way highway in Alberta (or anywhere), a Class 7 driver should signal clearly, accelerate to pass quickly and safely, avoid lingering in the blind spot, and then return to their lane only when they can see the truck's front bumper or headlights in their rearview mirror, giving plenty of space to the truck.

choices.text: Leave extra room before returning to their lane
Return to their lane once they have cleared the truck's front bumper
Return to their lane when signaled by the truck's headlights
Return to their lane when the truck is no longer visible in any of their rear-view mirrors
